sense danger: Dogs can often sense danger before people do, so they bark when strangers come near.
狗常常比人更早察覺危險，所以陌生人靠近時牠們會吠叫。
sense one's mood: When students walk into class, a good teacher can sense their mood just by looking at their faces.
學生走進教室時，好老師光看他們的臉就能察覺情緒。
sense that something is wrong: Whenever my mom is quiet at dinner, I can sense that something is wrong, even if she smiles.
每當媽媽在晚餐時很安靜，即使她在微笑，我也能感覺不對勁。
make sense: Your plan doesn't make sense to me; why would we leave at five in the morning?
你的計畫對我來說沒有道理；我們為什麼要早上五點出發？
come to one's senses: I hope he will come to his senses before he spends all his savings on that crazy plan.
我希望他在把所有積蓄花在那個瘋狂計畫之前能恢復理智。
sentence someone to prison: The judge decided to sentence the driver to prison for five years for causing the deadly accident.
法官決定判那名司機入獄五年，因為他造成了致命車禍。
be sentenced to death: The man who killed three people was sentenced to death by the court last week.
那名殺害三人的男子上週被法院判決，被判死刑。
a life sentence: He received a life sentence for the murder and will probably never leave prison again.
他因謀殺罪被判無期徒刑，可能再也無法出獄了。
serve a sentence: After he served a sentence of ten years, he wanted to start a new life and find honest work.
他服刑十年後，想重新開始生活、找份正當的工作。
separate fact from fiction: With so much fake news online, it is hard for young people to separate fact from fiction.
網路上假新聞這麼多，年輕人很難分辨事實與虛構。
separate from one's wife: After years of arguing, he decided to separate from his wife, though they did not divorce.
經過多年的爭吵，他決定與妻子分居，不過他們沒有離婚。
separate the two issues: We should separate the two issues and discuss the budget first, then talk about the schedule.
我們應該把兩個議題分開，先討論預算，再談時程。
separate the men from the boys: The final mountain stage will separate the men from the boys in this year's bike race.
最後的山路賽段將在今年的自行車賽中分出高下。
serve a purpose: Every rule in this school serves a purpose, even if it seems strange to you at first.
這所學校的每條規定都有用處，即使一開始你可能覺得奇怪。
serve the community: As a volunteer firefighter, he is proud to serve the community where he grew up.
身為義消，他很自豪能服務社區，那是他成長的地方。
serve time: His brother had to serve time in jail for stealing cars when he was young.
他哥哥年輕時因偷車而必須入獄服刑。
serve as a reminder: The old photos on the wall serve as a reminder of the hard times our grandparents went through.
牆上的老照片作為提醒，讓我們記得祖父母經歷過的艱苦歲月。
serve one right: He laughs at everyone and cheats on tests, so if he gets caught, it will serve him right.
他嘲笑所有人又考試作弊，所以如果他被抓到，真是活該。
serve notice: The landlord served notice that all tenants must leave the building by the end of March.
房東發出通知，所有房客必須在三月底前搬離大樓。
serve in the army: My grandfather had to serve in the army for two years before he became a teacher.
我爺爺在當老師之前必須從軍兩年。
serve a customer: It took the new waiter twenty minutes to serve a customer, so many people left the restaurant angry.
新來的服務生要花二十分鐘才能服務顧客，所以很多人氣沖沖地離開餐廳。
set a record: The young runner set a record by finishing the race in less than ten seconds.
那位年輕跑者創紀錄，以不到十秒的成績跑完比賽。
set an example: As the oldest child, you should set an example for your younger brothers and sisters.
身為家中老大，你應該為弟弟妹妹樹立榜樣。
set a goal: At the start of each year, I set a goal to read at least twenty English books.
每年年初，我都會設定目標，至少讀二十本英文書。
set the tone: The principal's warm opening speech set the tone for a friendly and relaxed meeting.
校長溫暖的開場致詞為這場友善輕鬆的會議定調。
set the table: Could you set the table with plates and forks while I finish cooking dinner?
我把晚餐煮完的時候，你可以擺餐桌、放好盤子和叉子嗎？
set foot in: It was the first time she had ever set foot in a foreign country, so she felt very excited.
這是她第一次踏進外國，所以她感到非常興奮。
set in stone: The schedule is not set in stone, so we can still change the date if it rains.
時程並非板上釘釘，所以如果下雨我們還是可以改日期。
set the stage for: The invention of the steam engine set the stage for the rapid growth of modern factories.
蒸汽機的發明為現代工廠的快速發展鋪路。
set a trap: The farmer set a trap near the chicken house to catch the fox that kept stealing eggs.
農夫在雞舍附近設陷阱，要抓那隻一直偷蛋的狐狸。
